E2-1

Policies
Latvenergo AS and the capital companies of the Group have
implemented a comprehensive approach to pollution management
and control. The approach is integrated into the overall
environmental management system, which is certified in
accordance with ISO 14001 at Latvenergo AS and Sadales tīkls AS.
Furthermore, Latvenergo AS maintains management systems for
labour protection (ISO 45001), energy management (ISO 50001)
and production quality (ISO 9001), which include elements for
pollution management and control and together form the
Integrated Management System.
In addition to the policies mentioned in the section General
Information and the third-party standards and initiatives followed
in their development, pollution management is also addressed by
the Environmental and Energy Management Policy. This policy
includes guiding principles for managing material IROs in the area

ST Shortterm

MT Medium
-term

LT Longterm

of pollution; it is integrated into the Sustainability Strategy for
2024–2026 and aims to prevent, reduce and control pollution and
its negative impacts, as well as to promote the responsible use of
resources. Information on the most senior level of management
responsible for the implementation of the policy, as well as a
description of how the interests of key stakeholders have been
taken into account in the policy development process, is provided in
the section General Information under Sustainability Management.
For a summary of Latvenergo’s policies on pollution issues (IROs)
management, see Policies adopted to manage material sustainability
matters in the section General Information.
The policies of Latvenergo Group aim to reduce air, water and soil
pollution, replace and minimise substances with potentially
negative impacts, and prevent incidents and emergencies and limit
their impact. The Group ensures compliance with the Industrial
Emissions Directive (IED), which establishes stringent environmental
emission limits for large combustion plants.

126


=== pdf p.127 ===
In Latvia, the IED requirements have been transposed into national
legislation through the Law on Pollution and corresponding regulations
of the Cabinet of Ministers. The Group’s CHPPs operate under
Category A permits for polluting activities, issued in line with the IED
framework and the application of Best Available Techniques (BAT).
Information on key pollutants is available in the permits for polluting
activities, which are accessible through the Public Data Register of the
State Environmental Service. The policies of the Latvenergo Group
cover the most significant groups of pollutants arising from the
Group’s operations and subject to applicable regulatory requirements
and permit conditions, including air emissions from combustion
processes, emissions to water and soil, as well as hazardous and other
chemicals. Pollution management is implemented in an integrated
manner, based on the requirements set out in applicable legislation,
permits for polluting activities, and best available techniques.
The primary focus of the policies is to reduce air pollution during
energy production processes. In this context, Latvenergo Group is
continuously upgrading its production facilities with the use of BAT
in accordance with EU requirements. The Group performs
emission monitoring and assessment to ensure compliance with
the threshold values and environmental quality standards set out
in the regulatory enactments.
The Group’s policies aimed at reducing pollution are aligned with
the objectives of the EU Green Deal and the EU Action Plan
Towards Zero Pollution for Air, Water and Soil, establishing the main
principles and approaches for environmental impact management:
• in the area of emission reduction, the control and reduction of
air pollutant emissions are foreseen through the application of
best available techniques and regular emissions monitoring
• in the area of water resource protection, the maintenance of
wastewater management processes is established, including
regular water quality monitoring, risk assessment, and
preventive measures to prevent water pollution
• in the area of soil and groundwater protection, regular site
monitoring, identification and management of pollution risks,
as well as the development and implementation of action plans
to prevent potential pollution risks are foreseen. In cases of
historical pollution, remediation measures are implemented in
accordance with the requirements of regulatory enactments
The improvement of the management of chemicals and mixtures is a
key component in controlling environmental pollution risks. By
minimizing the quantity of chemicals and mixtures used and stored,
and reducing their hazards, the risk of leakage and potential spillrelated consequences is significantly reduced. The Group uses
chemicals and mixtures solely to support its own production
processes and the operation of technological equipment. In order to

identify potential impacts and prevent or reduce the likelihood of harm,
procedures for the handling of chemicals and mixtures have been
established within the Group’s companies. The companies of the
Group comply with the requirements of applicable laws and regulations,
including the EU REACH (Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and
Restriction of Chemicals) Regulation, and keep abreast of legislative
changes regarding substances of very high concern (SVHC) and very
persistent and very bioaccumulative substances (vPvB). The
management of chemicals and mixtures is included in the Sustainability
Strategy of the Group to ensure a more responsible approach to
substitution and the phase-out of chemicals in the future.
With regard to the risk associated with the unexpected occurrence
of pollution at the Group’s sites, the Latvenergo Group applies an
incident prevention and management system based on a detailed
environmental risk assessment methodology, which enables the
systematic identification, assessment, and control of potential
risks. One type of environmental risk is related to the potential
leakage of chemicals and mixtures from production facilities,
distribution infrastructure, and storage sites, which may lead to
environmental contamination. To minimise these risks, the Group
has implemented a structured approach to emergency
management, including preventive measures and crisis action
plans. Procedures for liaising with emergency services and
environmental authorities have been set up, along with clear
protocols for communicating with stakeholders in the event of
incidents. The effectiveness of the systems and procedures
implemented under the policies is monitored and verified through
inspections carried out by the State Environmental Service, as well
as through independent external audits. In 2025, the Group was
subject to three inspections by the State Environmental Service.
The Group did not experience any significant environmental
incidents or receive any major reprimands from the controlling
institutions. An external audit that was conducted in 2025 confirmed
the effectiveness of the Integrated Management System of
Latvenergo Group and its ability to deliver the expected results in the
area of emergency management. The audit identified, as good
practice in incident and emergency management, the structured and
transparent accounting of waste flows, which reduces the risk of
environmental pollution, along with the systematic recording of
impact-related events and documented cooperation with the State
Environmental Service. This ensures effective monitoring of
incidents and coordinated action in emergency situations.
The Group’s policy includes regular environmental training for
employees and assessments of the environmental management
system’s effectiveness. Trained employees are equipped to
identify and address deviations from environmental standards,
manage risks, prevent incidents, and enhance environmental

practices. Internal and external audits are conducted to ensure
regulatory compliance and identify improvement opportunities.
Engagement with stakeholders, including national and local
authorities, is a critical component of the policy.
The above policy, as well as the Supplier Code of Conduct, covers
both the operations of Group companies themselves and upstream
and downstream value chain processes, ensuring a
comprehensive approach to addressing critical environmental
issues. The Group expects suppliers to take active steps in
reducing environmental pollution, including the reduction of
emissions to air and wastewater, the reduction of the volume and
hazardousness of chemicals and their mixtures, and systematic risk
assessment and management in environmental pollution matters.
Monitoring of the implementation and effectiveness of pollution
management policies is ensured within the framework of the
integrated management system, using certain indicators, regular
data collection, and analysis. Various tools and data sources are
used for monitoring, including automatic emission monitoring
systems, wastewater and groundwater quality control results,
laboratory analyses, environmental permit compliance control data
and internal accounting systems. Monitoring is carried out
according to the type of pollution: air emissions are monitored
continuously and additionally during periodic inspections, while
water and groundwater indicators are monitored periodically in
accordance with the requirements of regulatory enactments.
Supervision is conducted regularly at the day-to-day operational
level, through periodic internal inspections and management
reports, and within the framework of internal and external audits.
The effectiveness and progress of the policies are assessed by
comparing actual results with the established thresholds and the
Group’s objectives, analysing deviations and determining corrective
measures. Structural unit heads and environmental management
specialists are responsible for the supervision process within the
framework of their competences and division of responsibilities,
ensuring data quality, timely identification of deviations and
implementation of corrective measures, while senior management
evaluates the results and makes decisions on improving policies.
In 2025, Latvenergo AS received an overall score of 54 out of
100 points in the S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment.
The environmental dimension was assessed at 59 points,
significantly exceeding the industry average of 42 points and
confirming a targeted and consistent approach to environmental
management in line with good practice. The ‘Waste & Pollutants’
criterion received 42 points, exceeding the industry average of
40 points at the time of the assessment and confirming the
company’s systematic approach to pollution and waste
management in accordance with industry best practices.

E2-2

Actions and resources
Latvenergo’s approach to pollution management is based on
cooperation with both supply chain partners and customers. In the
upstream value chain, the Group works with fuel suppliers by setting
strict quality requirements for natural gas and other fuels, asthese
directly impact emission levels. Collaboration with equipment and
technology providers is also essential, focusing on the selection of
solutions with higher environmental performance and with waste
management companies to ensure proper recycling and disposal of
waste. In the downstream value chain, the Group actively engages
with end-users of electricity and thermal energy, promoting
energyefficient consumption. Cooperation with distribution system
users is also being enhanced through the implementation of smart
solutions and continuous improvements in network efficiency.
Latvenergo Group implements a comprehensive approach in pollution
management, which is based on the use of state-ofthe- art technologies
and sustainable resource management. During the reporting year, the
Group improved its activities and resources to reduce and control
pollution, with a particular focus on reducing emissions and improving
energy efficiency (for additional information see the sections Group
Strategy, Operating Segments and EU Taxonomy):
• Development of RES is a key area of focus for reducing
emissions – Latvenergo Group has actively invested in
increasing its RES generation capacity. In the reporting year,
approximately 2/3 of the total investment or EUR 548 million
was directed to the development of wind farms and solar parks.
At the end of the reporting year, the Group had solar and wind
parks with a total capacity of almost 646 MW under
construction. As a result, the total approved portfolio of new
renewable energy projects comprised 1,144 MW. Gradual
commissioning of the solar and wind parks is expected
between 2026 and 2027. This new RES capacity is expected
to generate an additional 2.2 TWh of electricity annually.
Alongside the new RES capacities, BESS projects are also
being developed. In the reporting year, two BESS projects with
a total capacity of 10.6 MW / 21.9 MWh were built. Meanwhile,
six BESS projects with a total capacity of 183.4 MW /
428.6 MWh are in the development stage. RES generation
facilities do not cause direct air, soil, or water pollution;
therefore, their development contributes to an overall
reduction in environmental pollution risks within the Group
• Generation modernisation and efficiency improvement is the
second key direction – In 2025, reconstruction work and
procurement procedures continued for the upgrade of the

hydropower units of the Daugava HPPs. In the reporting year,
EUR 17.8 million was invested in the assets of the Daugava
HPPs, of which EUR 11.1 million was invested in the
reconstruction programme of the hydropower units, which will
ensure their operability for more than 40 years. As a result of
the reconstruction of HPPs, the risks and volume of chemicals
leaks in hydro aggregates are reduced, and the use of oils with
lower environmental impact is being assessed. Investments in
distribution system assets amounted to EUR 172 million in the
reporting year, representing around 1/5 of the total investments
of the Group. About 25% of the distribution segment’s funds
were invested in the construction and reconstruction of power
lines and transformers, thus ensuring the high quality of network
services, technical performance and operational reliability
The Latvenergo Group plans to continue the development of RES,
the generation modernisation and efficiency improvements, as
well as the development of distribution system infrastructure in
accordance with the Medium-term Operational Strategy for 2022–
2026 and the Sustainability Strategy for 2024–2026, foreseeing
the implementation of these activities within the respective
strategic periods, with individual projects continuing to be
implemented in the subsequent years after 2026 (for additional
information, see the section Group Strategy).
Latvenergo Group applies an integrated pollution control and
management system to reduce the negative impact of air, water
and soil pollution. The Group complies with national and
international standards, including the requirements of BAT of the
EU, which help control emissions and optimise resource use.
Management of water resources and soil protection are ensured by
a well-developed monitoring system that helps identify potential
risks and implement necessary corrections promptly. Furthermore,
regular audits are performed to verify the effectiveness of policies
and compliance with them at all stages of operations.
A systematic approach is applied for pollution control at all
production sites, Latvenergo Group carries out regular
measurements and tests with the use of modern, verified metering
instruments that comply with the standards of BAT. The Group also
ensures compliance with the EU Taxonomy Regulation, which sets
out principles for pollution control and mitigation, and with the
criteria of the “causing no significant harm” principle.
In order to ensure suppliers’ compliance with the Group’s
requirements regarding pollution prevention and control,
Latvenergo also provides training for contractors, sets strict
requirements for their activities, and monitors compliance at the
Group’s production and infrastructure facilities. This approach
reinforces adherence to environmental protection regulations at
Latvenergo sites and reduces environmental risks.

During the reporting year, the Group continued to improve the
management of chemical substances and mixtures. A detailed
analysis of the substances and mixtures used was carried out, with
particular focus on the possibilities for substance substitution and
the identification of technically and economically justified
sustainable alternatives. At the same time, Latvenergo AS updated
its internal processes in line with the requirements of EU chemicals
regulation, which establishes stricter requirements for the
disclosure of information on hazardous substances, substances of
concern and substances of very high concern. In 2025, the
procedure for identifying chemical substances in use was
enhanced and the accounting of hazardous substances was
improved. In addition, a new structured process for the
procurement and evaluation of substances and mixtures was
introduced. This process strengthens a unified and transparent
approach to substance evaluation, ensuring consistent risk
assessment and the selection of the most appropriate solutions
already at the planning stage of procurement and use. During the
reporting year, a substance reporting procedure and a form for
evaluating substitution alternatives were also established.
In the area of ecosystem restoration, the Group is actively working
on mitigating the impacts of regular activities and on remediating
historical pollution. A historically polluted area is situated in
Aizkraukle, Dzelzceļa iela 10. It dates back to the mid-20th century,
when a prefabricated concrete factory was operating there. As a
result of the factory’s operation, the soil and groundwater were
contaminated with petroleum products to levels that exceed the
regulatory quality limits in an area of about 10.6 hectares. In order
to solve this problem, State Environmental Service, Aizkraukle
Municipality, in cooperation with Latvenergo AS, have
implemented several measures to determine the extent of pollution
and develop remediation solutions. In July 2025, the Ministry of
Climate and Energy and the State Environmental Service signed an
agreement to implement the project “Historically polluted site
remediation in Aizkraukle”. Following this, an inter‑institutional
working group was established, bringing together representatives
from the State Environmental Service, the Ministry of Climate and
Energy, Aizkraukle Municipality, and Latvenergo AS. In preparation
for the launch of remediation works, the State Environmental
Service initiated a supplier consultation in December 2025 as part
of the planned open tender for the remediation of the
contaminated site at Dzelzceļa Street 10, Aizkraukle. Latvenergo
AS actively contributed to the evaluation of the procurement
documentation by providing professional input on the proposed
requirements, technical solutions, and practical feasibility of the
remediation process.

=== pdf p.129 ===
In 2024–2025, Latvenergo AS completed the remediation of historical pollution at CHPP-2 by cleaning
the regenerative air heater section, where technological deposits had accumulated from earlier fuel‑oil
operations. The project included the removal and disposal of 2,486 tonnes of hazardous waste,
approximately 85% of which was recycled. The works were carried out through close cooperation
between internal structural units, significantly reducing future pollution risks within the CHPP-2 site.
Although at Group level quantitative emission reduction targets have been set only for air pollution, the
management of all types of emissions, including emissions to air and water, within the Group is ensured
in compliance with the requirements defined in environmental permits, the limit values established in
applicable legislation, and through the implementation of object-specific technical solutions. This
approach is aimed at preventing pollution at its source and avoiding significant environmental harm,
with a focus on improving process efficiency, ensuring control of pollutant concentrations, preventing
leakage and accident risks, and continuously enhancing monitoring and operational control systems.
To monitor and control pollution, the Group maintains an extensive network of monitoring systems, including:
• automatic emission measurement systems at production plants
• wastewater quality control systems
• a groundwater quality monitoring network
Regular funding is provided for the maintenance and upgrading of these systems, which includes both
technical maintenance and personnel training.
Implementing these measures contributes to achieving the objectives of Latvenergo Group’s pollution
management policy, ensuring their integration into the Group’s strategic planning and day-to-day
operations. The development of RES capacities and the modernization of existing generation assets
directly support the policy objective of reducing air pollution and GHG emissions, while also mitigating
pollution risks throughout the entire asset life cycle. Investments in the reconstruction of HPPs and in
electricity distribution infrastructure contribute to pollution prevention and control by reducing the
likelihood of hazardous substance releases and improving energy efficiency. In addition, cooperation
with supply chain partners and end users ensures that pollution management requirements are applied
beyond the Group’s direct operations, thereby strengthening the achievement of policy objectives
across upstream and downstream value chains.
E2-3

Targets
Based on national laws and regulations, the relevant authorities issue environmental permits for all
Latvenergo Group production facilities, which set specific emission and effluent limits for air
pollutants. In addition to these requirements, the internal environmental management standards of
the Group may set even stricter thresholds that reflect best available industry practices. The aim of
this approach is not only to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements but also to reduce
negative environmental impacts by promoting sustainable development. All target indicators are
regularly monitored with the use of an integrated environmental monitoring system. Once a year, a
detailed analysis of the target parameters is carried out and, where necessary, they are adjusted to
take into account changes in technology, legislation or the specific nature of the Group's operations.
Regular reports on the achievement of target parameters are provided to the management and
stakeholders, ensuring the transparency and control of processes. To ensure that the target
parameters are met, Latvenergo Group allocates financial resources to research, the introduction of
advanced technologies, and personnel training. The companies of the Group also collaborate with

national and international environmental protection and sectors' organisations to use best practices
and improve efficiency in achieving their objectives.
Latvenergo Group constitutes the framework for setting the targets. The sections About the Group and
Operating Segments provide information on the geographical scope of Latvenergo Group’s economic
activities and its main operational sites. The targets mainly relate to the Group’s own operations.
The targets have been set voluntarily, taking into account industry guidelines and available research,
technological capabilities and economic justification, the local context and existing infrastructure, as
well as stakeholder expectations. For information on stakeholder involvement in the target-setting
process of the strategy, please refer to the section General Information. In the area of pollution,
Latvenergo Group has defined three key targets. The targets include both quantitative objectives with
defined achievement timelines and qualitative objectives and measures that describe the Group’s
approach to pollution prevention and risk management in areas where precise numerical indicators are
not applicable.

=== pdf p.130 ===
The commitment to reduce emissions of pollutants into the air aims
to reduce the quantity of emissions per unit of energy generated.
Emissions per unit of energy generated, or specific emissions,
reflect the efficiency of the Group’s existing processes, the technical
solutions implemented by CHPPs to reduce pollutant emissions, and
efforts to increase the RES portfolio through the development of
wind and solar power plants and partially replacing fossil fuels.
Emissions reduction is driven by several factors: modernised
generation processes, more efficient fuel use, and the ongoing
partial substitution of fossil fuels with RES. In this context, the
Group’s targeted development of wind and solar power plants is of
particular importance, enabling the gradual reduction of fossil
energy use and, consequently, emission intensity. The Group will
continue to promote the development of renewable energy-based
generation capacity (wind and solar), increase the efficiency of
energy generation and maximise the use of RES. Latvenergo Group
has set a target to reduce air pollutant emissions by measuring the
amount of carbon monoxide (CO) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) emitted
per unit of energy generated. Emissions per unit of energy generated,
or specific emissions, reflect the efficiency of the Group’s existing
processes, the technical solutions implemented by CHPPs to reduce
pollutant emissions, and efforts to increase the renewable energy
portfolio through the development of wind and solar power plants.
At the same time, the Group also extends its targets to the
prevention and control of emissions to the water environment and
soil protection, ensuring the long-term reduction of pollutantspecific loads in both environmental media. Measures for water
resource protection include both the reduction of wastewater
volumes and pollutant concentrations through the implementation
of technical improvements. As wastewater volumes decrease, the
potential pollutant loads and their overall impact on the aquatic
environment are proportionally reduced. These measures are
complemented by robust risk management, including the
prevention of leaks of chemicals and technological fluids, the
implementation of strict storage safety requirements, regular
monitoring, and technological solutions that reduce the release of
pollutants into wastewater. At the same time, the Group also
ensures soil quality protection by managing pollution risks that
could arise from leaks of chemical substances, fuels, or other
potentially harmful materials. Secure and leak-proof storage of
substances is ensured, the technical condition of equipment is
regularly monitored, and preventive engineering solutions are
implemented to prevent leakage. The Group is gradually
substituting hazardous chemicals with less harmful alternatives
and reducing their overall use, thereby mitigating potential adverse
impacts on soil environments and ensuring that both water and soil
pollution risks are managed through a unified, integrated approach.

“Mission 0” in the area of the environment – in line with the EU Action
Plan “Towards Zero Pollution for Air, Water and Soil”, the Latvenergo
Group, as one of its priorities in the area of pollution prevention, sets
the objective of preventing cases of significant environmental harm,
which entails an integrated approach to environmental risk
management and pollution control across all environmental media,
including air, water and soil. Within the Latvenergo Group, major
environmental pollution cases are defined as events that, in
accordance with the risk appetite set out in the Risk Register, are
classified as exceeding that threshold. The Group’s risk appetite in
the environmental matter stipulates the avoidance of environmental
pollution events that would result in a material reputational or
financial impact. Cases are considered major where substantial
environmental pollution with long-term consequences is identified;
material breaches of environmental requirements are detected
during external inspections; administrative sanctions are imposed or
criminal proceedings are initiated for environmental pollution; or
additional operational restrictions are imposed due to environmental
requirements. This commitment reflects the Group’s efforts to
prevent environmental pollution by identifying and mitigating
potential risks, ensuring wastewater treatment, the safe storage of
liquids and chemical substances, and adapting production
processes to reduce the release of pollutants into the environment.
This approach complements the Group’s objectives for reducing
emissions and pollutant loads to air, water and soil.
Progress towards the targets achievement is primarily assessed
against the predefined target values rather than in comparison to
historical baselines. This approach was chosen as it aligns more
effectively with the Group’s strategy and allows for greater
flexibility in responding to developments within the energy sector.
The targets are pursued through specific measures, including the
development of RES, improvements in production efficiency, and
systematic risk management. Results achieved in 2025:
• emissions of pollutants into the air – NOx and CO per unit of energy
generated emissions per unit of energy produced continued to
decrease and reached 0.07 kg/MWh NOx and 0.04 kg/MWh CO,
respectively. Although emissions have decreased, they are above
the Group's 2030 target of 0.03 kg/MWh or -50% compared to
0.07 kg/MWh of NOx in 2022 and 0.02 kg/MWh or -50%
compared to 0.04 kg/MWh of CO in 2022. This points to the need
for further emission reduction measures, more efficient production
processes and the development of renewable energy generation
capacity, which will contribute to the overall reduction of GHG
emissions and support the development of sustainable energy
• number of cases of significant environmental damage – as in the
previous reporting period, no cases of significant environmental
damage were recorded in the 2025. This demonstrates the

Group’s effective environmental management, pollution
prevention measures and compliance with environmental
protection requirements across all environmental aspects,
including air, water, and soil
• reducing pollution risks related to chemicals – in 2025, the Group
continued to strengthen the management of chemical substances
and mixtures by conducting a detailed analysis of substances in
use, identifying substitution options, and introducing a structured
process for the procurement, accounting and evaluation of
chemical substances. Internal procedures were updated in line
with the requirements of EU chemical legislation
In addition to the established environmental protection measures,
the Group is working purposefully to maintain water resource
quality, ensuring that wastewater complies with the limit values set
out in applicable regulatory requirements prior to discharge.
Emission limits for wastewater pollutants are set in line with
national and EU legislation to protect water resources and
ecosystems. Monitoring frequency, methods, and requirements
are determined by the competent national authority.
To prevent cases of significant environmental damage and ensure
soil protection, the Group has developed the internal Environmental
Risk Assessment Methodology, assesses environmental risks in all
activities and processes, ensures close monitoring and control of
technological processes, sets requirements for contractors and
monitors their implementation, and fosters the competence of the
responsible employees. Storage and handling of chemicals and
mixtures is carried out in a manner that is safe for humans and the
environment, with design and technical solutions to prevent
leakages. To promote safety and environmental protection, the Group
will continue and strengthen its environmentalrisk management, which
includes risk identification, assessment and mitigation.
E2-4

Pollution of air, water and soil
Emissions of air pollutants
Emissions of air pollutants by Latvenergo Group are directly
affected by the type of fuel used, the scale of energy production
and the efficiency of technologies. The Group’s production
facilities use three main fuels, each with its own characteristic
emissions profile. The Group’s air emissions primarily originate
from large combustion plants – Latvenergo AS CHPPs and Liepaja
plants. Other emission sources within the Group are considered
insignificant; therefore, a detailed breakdown by source type,
sector, or geographical area is not applicable.
130


=== pdf p.131 ===
Natural gas used at the CHPPs of Latvenergo AS and the Liepaja
plants emits NOx and CO. In addition to NOx and CO emissions,
diesel fuel used as emergency fuel at the CHPPs also emits sulphur
dioxide (SO2), particulate matter and hydrocarbons during storage.
Meanwhile, wood used at the Liepaja plants emits NOx, CO, and
particulate matter. Modern technologies are used to reduce
emissions, including electronic filters and multicyclones installed
at the Liepaja plants to capture particulate matter. In addition,
automatic combustion control systems in CHPPs equipment, lowNOx emission burners, and other technological solutions ensure an
optimal and controlled combustion process, as well as operation in
cogeneration mode further enhances fuel efficiency and reduces
emissions per unit of energy produced.
In 2025, the total volume of pollutant emissions within the Group
decreased, primarily due to lower energy production volumes at
the CHPPs. SO₂ emissions remained at a low level, as diesel fuel
was hardly used at the CHPPs during the reporting year. In
previous years – particularly in 2022 and 2023 – diesel fuel was
used periodically due to high natural gas prices and uncertainty
regarding supply. The volume of volatile organic compound
emissions increased slightly, primarily in connection with diesel
fuel tank inspections carried out during the reporting year and the
associated fuel reloading operations.
Emission quantities from combustion plants have been determined
using emission monitoring data or emission factors obtained in
accordance with laws and regulations.
Pollutants discharged into surface water

into the environment (mainly CHPP-2, where the largest volume of
wastewater within the Group is generated during production
processes) are subject to regular effluent quality testing to ensure
compliance with regulatory requirements. The testing analyses
key pollutant parameters, including chemical oxygen demand,
suspended solids and other potential pollutants.
The Group’s operations have not identified any direct sources of
pollution that would result in emissions into the soil. However,
recognizing the importance of this environmental aspect, the Group
monitors groundwater quality at its facilities to detect potential risks
promptly and prevent any possible contamination. In cases of
historical pollution, remediation measures are implemented and
planned in compliance with regulatory requirements (for information
on historical pollution, see the section Actions and Resources).
The use of microplastics in the Group’s activities and operations is
insignificant, as this material is not typically used in electricity and
thermal energy generation and distribution processes.
The amount of pollution emitted is determined in accordance with
the methods laid down in the regulatory enactments, the relevant
permit, and analyses carried out by accredited laboratories or
standardised calculations. The use of direct measurements is a
priority; however, in cases where this is not possible, calculation
methodologies are applied, with data sources clearly indicated.
Collection of data on emissions and the processing thereof takes
place on several levels:
• automatic data collection from continuous monitoring systems
• regular sampling and laboratory tests

The Group’s main sources of wastewater are production facilities
that utilize water for technological purposes, as well as domestic
wastewater. The facilities of the Group that discharge wastewaters

Where direct measurements are not possible or economically feasible,
calculation methods are used. The main reasons for using calculation
methods are the disproportionately high costs associated with direct

NOX , CO, SO2 and other emissions into the air
Unit
NOx

measurements relative to the volume and impact of emissions, as well
as the approach to specific emissions outlined in regulatory
enactments. Two primary calculation methods are applied:
• calculation of the quantity of emissions with the use of
emission factors (values that describe the ratio of the quantity
of a pollutant to a parameter that characterises an activity
related to the emission of that pollutant)
• mass balance calculations
To calculate air pollutant emissions, the Group uses emission
factors that are derived from reliable and recognised data sources
and databases that are used in industry practice and comply with
regulatory requirements. Emission factors for combustion plants
are determined by the regulation of the Cabinet of Ministers No. 17
Regulations on the Control of Air Pollution from Combustion Plants,
while the general approach to the selection of emission factors is
determined by the regulatory enactments on the development of
emission limit projects for stationary sources of pollution.
Data is stored in secure databases and record-keeping systems
that ensure traceability and availability for analysis and reporting.
This approach allows for trend identification and emission source
analysis, ensuring compliance with legislation and sustainability
targets. A multi-level control system ensures data quality, with
regular internal checks and audits, including ISO 14001 and ISO
9001 certification processes and inspections by the State
Environmental Service in connection with the submission of
environmental statistical reports (2-Air, 2-Water). This integrated
approach ensures the accuracy and reliability of the data.
Latvenergo Group performs an environmental pollutant inventory in
accordance with EC Regulation No. 166/2006, On the Establishment
of a European Pollutant Release and Transfer Register.

Substances of concern and substances of very high concern
Companies of the Group do not distribute, sell or export chemicals.

E2-6
Pollution-related risks and the financial effects thereof
The Group has carried out a comprehensive analysis of the
material risks associated with pollution and their expected financial
impact over different periods of time. The Group’s risk and
opportunity assessment methodology includes the magnitude of
the financial impact as one of the assessment criteria by
determining a range of financial loss or gain for each degree of
materiality. The main risks identified are related to emissions from
combustion equipment (at the Latvenergo CHPPs and the Liepāja
generation facilities) in the process of electricity and heat
generation, the potential release of pollutants into water (at the
Group’s HPPs), as well as potential historical pollution at the
Group's sites (see table Material impacts, risks and opportunities
and section Actions and resources).

In addition to the aforementioned, the Group anticipates potential
costs related to the remediation of historical pollution. In 2025,
Latvenergo AS established a provision for environmental protection
and remediation measures. This provision is intended to cover
potential remediation actions to mitigate environmental pollution
risks associated with the historically contaminated area of the former
Aizkraukle reinforced concrete plant, located on property owned by
Latvenergo AS, and the potential threat it poses to the safety of the
Plavinas HPP structures. In 2025, provisions were revised in line with
the latest cost estimates for remediation activities, reaching a total
amount of EUR 2.3 million. During the reporting period, provisions of
EUR 1.4 million were recognised for the disposal of asbestos waste
at CHPP-2, taking into account environmental protection
requirements and the need for the gradual dismantling of historical,
non-operational equipment and structures containing asbestos
materials (see Note 27 Provisions in the Financial Statements
section). To mitigate pollution risks, the cleaning and removal of
historical waste from the CHPP-2 technological sludge storage
facility, initiated in 2024, was completed during the reporting year.

The waste originated from the use of heavy fuel oil as a fuel. The
total cost of the project amounted to EUR 0.78 million.
No serious incidents or pollution were detected during the
reporting period and therefore no operating or capital expenditure
related to such was incurred.
E2-6
Opportunities related to pollution prevention and control
The Group is continuously introducing new technologies and
sustainable solutions to reduce the impact of pollution on the
environment while promoting sustainable growth. Strategic
investment in green technologies, innovative production
processes, advanced pollution control methods and chemical
management not only improves the efficiency of resource use but
also contributes to cost optimisation and strengthening of the
Group’s competitiveness.

In the event that a pollution risk is identified, the Group assesses
the need for remediation of the respective site by determining the
extent of pollution, selecting appropriate solutions, and planning
the associated costs, while also evaluating the broader impact on
the environment and society and implementing appropriate
measures where necessary.
In the short term, the expected financial impact is relatively limited
and is primarily related to the investments required to maintain and
upgrade emission control systems. The activities currently
implemented by the Group in the area of pollution prevention and
control and the operation of its production facilities comply with
the applicable BAT guidelines and the threshold values determined.
In the medium term, the Group foresees the need to continue
investing in the modernisation of production processes, which may
require a moderate level of financial resources. In the longer term,
however, it is expected that regulatory changes, technological
developments and market requirements may require moderate to
significant investments to ensure the transition to environmentally
friendly technologies. At the same time, such investments may also
generate positive financial impacts in the long term by reducing
future risks and potential costs.

E4-1

Transition plan
The energy transition process implemented by Latvenergo Group
provides for a structural and technological transformation of
energy production, distribution systems and consumption, thus
ensuring an energy-efficient, sustainable and environmentally
friendly energy supply model, and integrating the conservation of
biodiversity as an essential aspect of sustainability.
The conservation of biodiversity goes hand in hand with the limiting
climate change; therefore, the Group seeks in its operations to
ensure a balanced development of renewable energy generation
capacities, improving energy infrastructure and distribution systems,
while taking into account economic aspects, ensuring accessible
energy for society and helping preserve nature.
Several policies have been introduced at Latvenergo Group where
aspects of biodiversity and ecosystem protection are integrated
(see Policies). They set out the Group's operational principles on
the preservation of nature, including requirements for
environmental impact assessment, ensuring the protection of
biotopes and species, and the planning and implementation of
preventive and impact-mitigating measures in the Group's
operations, including project development.
The main document of the transformation process in the field of
biodiversity is the Biodiversity Transition Plan for 2026–2028,
developed in 2025, which sets out the main directions of action,
specific measures, objectives and a methodological framework for
managing biodiversity and ecosystems in the Group's operations. It
also defines implementation responsibilities and the mechanisms for
monitoring and reporting. The Biodiversity Transition Plan was
approved by the Management Board of Latvenergo AS after the
reporting period (March 2026).
In order to ensure consistent, transparent and long-term effective
integration of biodiversity in the Group's operations, the actions
set out in the Biodiversity Transition Plan are structured from the
Group's strategic level to their practical implementation at the
asset level. This framework ensures a clear link between the
Group's strategy, priorities and specific measures in assets, while
enabling flexible adaptation to new data, scientific insights and
regulatory changes.
1. Strategic integration at the Group level – Biodiversity
considerations are integrated into Latvenergo Group's strategy,
policies and governance processes. This level sets the overall
direction and ambition, ensuring that biodiversity issues are an
integral part of the Group's business model and development

strategy, including investment decision-making, setting priorities,
and risk and resilience assessment.
At this level, overarching objectives are set and compliance with
EU and international frameworks is ensured, including the
Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, the EU
Biodiversity Strategy for 2030 and the UN SDGs. Decision-making
takes place at the level of the Group's management and the boards
of subsidiaries, ensuring accountability and oversight.
2. Priorities and objectives until 2028 – The Group's strategic
ambitions are specified in defined, time-bound objectives and
priorities until 2028. This level ensures the link between strategic
directions and practical implementation, determining the priority
impacts on biodiversity based on the IRO assessment, identifying
which asset groups require special focus, and defining the results
to be achieved in the medium term.
At this level, indicators, baselines and achievable results are
defined, and a roadmap is developed, which provides for a gradual
transition from pilot projects to full-scale solutions. At the same
time, this framework provides the opportunity to regularly review
objectives and, if necessary, adjust them, taking into account
monitoring results, new information and scientific developments.
3. Practical implementation and improvements in assets – The
implementation of practical measures at the project and asset level
includes the application of the impact mitigation hierarchy
(avoidance, minimisation, restoration, compensation), as well as
the implementation of specific technical, operational and
management solutions. Both mandatory and voluntary monitoring
measures and the evaluation of their results are ensured,
promoting continuous improvement of operations and evidencebased decision-making.
At this level, Latvenergo Group measures are implemented that link
direct operations, the supply chain impact and a broader
ecosystem and societal perspective:
• direct operations (own operations) – planning new projects
applying the impact mitigation hierarchy, as well as mitigating
of the impact of new and existing projects, biotope restoration,
species protection measures, support for fish migration and
the introduction of nature-inclusive infrastructure solutions
(for more information, see the section Actions and Resources)
• supply chain impact (upstream value chain) – sustainable
supply chain management, reducing GHG emissions and
progress towards climate neutrality, responsible procurement
practices and cooperation with key suppliers to reduce the
Group's indirect impact on biodiversity and promote the
efficient use of resources in diversity initiatives

• ecosystems and society (downstream value chain) – the
conservation and restoration of natural areas, the development
of nature-based solutions, partnerships and cooperation with
local communities and other stakeholders. Biodiversity
considerations are integrated into the Group's policies and
decision-making processes. In Latvia and Lithuania, regulatory
provisions provide for community payments to municipalities
and the nearest homesteads in the vicinity of wind farms,
thereby strengthening the involvement of local communities
and ensuring them direct benefits
This approach ensures systematic and structured management of
biodiversity, as well as a clear link between strategic objectives
and practically implementable measures, ensuring regular
progress assessment and timely adjustment of actions. It forms a
dynamic transition plan, which is regularly improved based on
acquired experience and new insights.
The operational strategy of Latvenergo Group has been developed
taking the physical, transition and systemic risks to biodiversity
and ecosystems into account. The Biodiversity Transition Plan for
2026–2028 defines in greater detail the Group's approach to
managing of biodiversity issues. It is based on the analysis carried
out by the Group regarding the resilience of the strategy and
business model in relation to the development of the status of
biodiversity and ecosystems, as well as the objectives set in local,
national and global policy and regulation.
The main physical risks are related to Latvenergo Group's
economic operations, including the impact of operating and
constructing Daugava HPPs and RES (biomass, wind and solar)
energy generation facilities, as well as managing electricity
transmission line corridors, on landscapes, natural ecosystems,
and the condition of species and biotopes. In addition to the
aforementioned factors, climate change is one of the causes of the
decline in biodiversity; therefore, Latvenergo Group continues to
develop energy production from RES and to modernise electricity
infrastructure, while striving to ensure a balance between climate
change mitigation and the conservation of biodiversity.
Transition risks include the need to adapt to stricter nature
protection requirements, including the EU Green Deal initiatives
and the EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030. Requirements for the
protection of species and biotopes are being strengthened, and
the Natura 2000 network of protected areas is being expanded,
which may cause additional challenges for the development of
new RES projects and the operation of infrastructure. When
developing new projects and maintaining existing infrastructure,
Latvenergo Group assesses the potential impact on biodiversity
already at the planning stage, considering environmental
protection principles and regulatory requirements.

=== pdf p.135 ===
Systemic risks are related to broader changes in ecosystems and
the availability of natural resources, which may affect the Group's
operations in the long term. They may take the form of a decline in
biodiversity, ecosystem degradation or deterioration of ecosystem
services, which in turn may affect the availability of natural
resources, infrastructure development opportunities, land use and
project implementation. Such risks may also arise in the Group's
upstream and downstream value chain, for example, in relation to
the sustainable availability of natural resources, the impact of
suppliers' activities on biodiversity, and the increasing demands of
society and other stakeholders regarding nature protection.
Latvenergo Group primarily analyses its impact on biodiversity and
ecosystems in its own operations, while also assessing, as far as
possible, the impact in the upstream and downstream parts of the
Group's value chain. The analysis encompasses both risk
identification and opportunity assessment, including asset
optimization, the promotion of sustainable use of natural resources,
and public engagement.
The Group's Biodiversity Transition Plan is based on a clear vision
of the development of the energy sector and society's
expectations for the future, as well as on the assumption that
Latvenergo Group's operations impact the environment at various
levels – both directly and indirectly, both locally and cumulatively.
Several important assumptions have been used for the
development of the Plan:
• availability of financial resources – sufficient funding will be
available for initiatives, ensuring the implementation of actions
and long-term budget stability
• changes in regulation – stricter environmental protection
requirements may affect project development; therefore,
timely adaptation and ensured compliance are necessary
• cooperation with stakeholders – cooperation with communities
and organisations promotes the introduction of sustainable
practices and public acceptance
• technological development – innovations and new
technologies will enable the improvement of environmental
impact management solutions
• increasing demand for sustainable solutions – this drives the
Group's operations and will support measures for the
conservation of natural capital
In the resilience analysis, the Group assesses the risks,
dependencies, impacts and opportunities arising from changes in
biodiversity and ecosystems, taking into account short-term,
medium-term and long-term perspectives.

The analysis shows that Latvenergo Group's operations impact
biodiversity both directly in its own infrastructure projects and
indirectly through value chains. The main impacts are related to the
development and maintenance of energy infrastructure, including
the operation of RES projects and HPPs and the management of
electricity distribution networks. These activities may cause
challenges in land use and ecosystem quality, such as habitat
fragmentation, transformation of biotopes and the spread of
invasive species. In addition, operational emissions and indirect
impacts put pressure on ecosystems. The most significant risks
within supply chains are related to the extraction of natural
resources and raw materials, including logging, which is necessary
for the construction and maintenance of equipment. At the same
time, the development of renewable energy projects reduces
pressure on ecosystems in the long term and promotes the
conservation of biodiversity.

taken into account in developing the Group's policies, including the
Biodiversity Transition Plan for 2026–2028, and it promotes the
coherence of activities and informed decision-making. Main areas
of activity:

The analysis also identified the main risks and opportunities. The
most significant challenges are related to the timely acquisition of
environmental permits, compliance with regulatory requirements
and the provision of monitoring, including aspects of habitat and
species protection. Physical risks are related to changes in
ecosystems and the transformation of natural processes, which may
affect hydrological regimes, biological cycles and the continuity of
asset operations. Transition risks include increasing demands from
society, investors and regulators on responsible management of
natural capital. Timely and targeted management helps mitigate
reputational risks, facilitates project implementation and improves
the Group's operational efficiency, financial results and reputation.

• participation in international organisations – involvement in
international working groups, exchange of experience and
implementation of best practices

Latvenergo implements impact and risk mitigation measures
across all time frames. In the short term, immediate issues are
addressed, such as the optimisation of asset maintenance
practices and habitat protection. In the medium term,
improvements and projects are implemented, including the
restoration of biotopes, the introduction of nature-friendly
infrastructure solutions and the provision of sustainable supply
chain management. In the long term, strategic actions are planned
to ensure operational resilience and a balance between energy
development and nature protection, such as creating biologically
valuable habitats, developing innovations and technologies for bird
protection and for improving the efficiency of renewable energy
facilities, and attracting public funding for biodiversity measures.
Processes have been introduced at the Group to ensure
consultation and cooperation with stakeholders, in order to
consider their opinions and expertise both in project development
and in the implementation of biological resource, habitat and
species protection measures, including more extensive activities
of the Group. The information obtained within this cooperation is

• involvement of local communities in project planning and
operation – dialogue with communities and municipalities on
the impact of RES projects, evaluating the information received
and potential adaptation options (see S3 Affected
Communities)
• education and public awareness – educational programmes
and campaigns on sustainable lifestyles and biodiversity
• cooperation with stakeholders – environmental institutions,
specialists and non-governmental organisations – to develop
solutions for the conservation of biodiversity and strengthen
knowledge exchange

The implementation of the Biodiversity Transition Plan is ensured
through the Group’s existing resources, including employee
competencies, internal processes, management systems and
available data, as well as through the acquisition of information and
knowledge via cooperation with non-governmental organizations,
environmental authorities, experts and local communities. The
estimated costs for the implementation of the Plan’s activities over
the period 2026–2028 are indicatively assessed at approximately
EUR 25 million. Of this amount, around EUR 19 million relates to the
natural resource tax on water use for electricity generation at
hydropower plants and to the fish restocking programme, while
approximately EUR 3.5 million represents capital investments,
covering both compliance with mandatory obligations and the
implementation of voluntary activities.
This systematic and well-founded approach to managing of
biodiversity strengthens the Group's operational resilience,
improves asset sustainability, and increases investment
predictability and reputation, while ensuring public support and the
reduction of long-term regulatory and financial risks

Policies
In addition to the policies listed in the section General Information
and the third-party standards and initiatives followed in their
development, biodiversity and ecosystems topics are also covered by:

• the Environmental and Energy Management Policy, which

Group's approach to integrating biodiversity into energy

impact mitigation hierarchy and provides timely impact
assessments within the development of new RES projects,
targeted measures to improve biotopes and habitats in existing

international environmental protection standards and EU initiatives,
including the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework

For a summary of Latvenergo's policies on managing biodiversity
and ecosystems issues (IROs), see Policies adopted to manage
material sustainability matters in the section General Information.
The Group has identified and assessed the primary direct factors
on biodiversity:
• climate change – in connection with energy production processes
• changes in land use and deterioration of biotope quality –
associated with the development of energy infrastructure,
including alterations in the use of freshwater resources within
the Daugava River basin
• direct exploitation – the use of natural resources for energy
production
• pollution – arising from production processes
• other factors – such as the physical impact caused by the
location of infrastructure facilities
The Group implements well-defined policies at several levels:

• environmental risk management – the Group uses a structured
environmental risk assessment system, which includes five
levels of risk, ranging from unacceptably high to insignificant.
For each level of risk, specific timeframes for action and
management measures are definedIn the event of unacceptably
high risk, immediate intervention is carried out, while in the case
of lower risk, preventive measures are implemented within
technically and economically feasible timeframes
• environmental impact assessment – EIA are carried out at all
major projects. Wind project development is assessed across
the Baltic states and in different landscapes – forest land,
developed wetlands and agricultural land – to diversify risks
and boost renewable energy generation capacity. These
assessments include detailed biodiversity surveys, which
include species and habitat studies, as well as studies of
ornithofauna and bats, as a result of which expert opinions are
developed regarding locations where wind farms should be
built. An integral part of the EIA involves developing monitoring
plans for the evaluation and protection of birds and bats, as
well as implementing measures to mitigate the impact of wind
farms and their associated infrastructure on nature

These strategic documents provide a unified framework for the
biodiversity conservation activities of the Group, ensuring a
systematic and science-based approach to ecosystem protection
while contributing to sustainable development. Information on the
most senior level of management responsible for the
implementation of the policy, as well as a description of how the
interests of key stakeholders have been taken into account in the
policy development process, is provided in the section General
Information under Sustainability Management. The Group
implements a structured and targeted approach to the
conservation and restoration of biodiversity, in alignment with

• environmental mitigation and compensation measures – the
Group implements measures to conserve biodiversity (see the
table Objectives and key performance indicators for mitigation
measures):
– natural fish restocking programmes in the Daugava River
basin, maintaining populations of anadromous and native
fish species, improving the ecological quality of rivers and
assessing opportunities to improve fish migration
– measures to protect birds on the grounds of wind farms,
including safety mechanisms to reduce the risk of

– measures to compensate for forest areas used for the

• preventive approach – the Group takes a preventive approach
to environmental protection, which includes early identification
of risks at the project planning stage, regular monitoring and
control, collaboration with environmental experts and
scientists, and training and educating personnel on
environmental issues
The Group’s biodiversity and ecosystem policies are designed to
purposefully manage and mitigate the company’s significant
impact on biodiversity and ecosystems. The Group rigorously
assesses the impact of existing and planned activities on
biodiversity and implements both statutory and voluntary
measures to reduce the impact on protected areas, species and
habitats. The main environmental interactions in the Group’s
activities are related to the Daugava River basin and its
hydrological regime. The cascade of the Daugava HPPs, with a total
capacity of 1,558 MW, is the Group’s largest renewable energy
source. At the same time, the Group continues to develop new wind
and solar energy capacities, which reached 498 MW by the end of
2025, thus increasing the significance of these interactions.
Latvenergo Group implements a systematic approach to ecosystem
and biodiversity management in the following main areas:
• management of Daugava River basin ecosystems
• impact management of wind, solar energy and BESS projects
• maintenance of electricity distribution infrastructure
For more detailed information on the management of the
aforementioned areas, see the section Actions and resources.
Latvenergo Group's diversity and ecosystems policies directly link
strategy with practical action, enabling the management of
material dependencies and physical and transition risks and
opportunities. A systematic approach, with risk assessment,

preventive measures, compensation and monitoring, promotes
operational resilience, sustainable asset management and public
trust, while ensuring the Group's compliance with climate and
sustainability objectives. Such integration makes diversity and
ecosystems aspects an integral part of Latvenergo Group's
decision-making and energy transition processes.
Currently, the Group is not directly engaged in active cooperation
with suppliers regarding biodiversity protection. However, in line
with the Suppliers Code of Conduct, suppliers are expected to
implement proactive measures for the preservation and protection
of biodiversity. This includes not only assessing the impact of
activities on protected areas, species and habitats but also mitigating
these impacts by meeting strict environmental protection standards.
Suppliers must assume responsibility for the sustainability of their
operations and take appropriate measures to preserve biodiversity.
The Group promotes collaboration with suppliers who can certify
the origin of their raw materials and the environmental
compatibility of their extraction methods. For instance, the use of
wood as a fuel requires transparent documentation that confirms
the wood’s origin and extraction methods and ensures that the
wood used is sourced from sustainably managed and certified
forests, in compliance with international environmental standards
and the requirements of the Renewable Energy Directive.
Latvenergo Group continues to strive towards responsible
resource management, pursuing goals that ensure sustainable
development, environmental protection and a responsible
approach to both the operations of the Group and the interests of
society. The Group’s strategy includes the sustainable use of
resources and the development of supply chains, which promotes
the protection of the environment and the development of a
sustainable energy system.
Latvenergo Group addresses biodiversity conservation not only
from an environmental perspective but also from a social one.
Being aware that ecosystem and biodiversity management policies
have a direct impact on stakeholders, the Group develops and
implements policies that promote a socially responsible approach
to natural resource management and ensure a positive impact on
local communities. The Group’s biodiversity and ecosystem
policies encompass the assessment and management of social
impacts. The Group's operations have to assess and address the
potential impact on local communities. Social aspects are
assessed in relation to:

• economic activities related to the use of natural resources
The policies outline specific courses of action to mitigate social
impacts, including compensation mechanisms, provision of
alternative resources, and community involvement in decisionmaking. Further information on community engagement, education,
and cooperation with stakeholders is provided in the section
Actions and resources.
Latvenergo Group's set of policies on sites located in or near areas
sensitive in terms of biodiversity provides for the responsible and
sustainable use of natural resources. These policies establish the
fundamental principles thus ensuring the maximum reduction of
negative impact on biotopes, species and ecosystems, with
particular attention paid to endangered species and biotopes.
Where necessary, they also provide for compensatory measures
to balance the impact.
Latvenergo Group's approach to sustainable land use is based on
several fundamental principles, including multifunctional land use,
revitalisation of areas, efficient use of land and the conservation of
biodiversity.
The restoration of former industrial areas and their use for energy
development play a significant role in Latvenergo’s land
management practice. For example, former peat extraction areas
are used for the development of wind farms, as demonstrated by
the Laflora Energy wind power project in the former peat extraction
areas of Kaigu bog, with a planned capacity of 109 MW. Such an
approach reduces the impact on natural and agricultural areas,
while promoting environmentally friendly development.
Latvenergo Group’s approach to deforestation issues in new RES
assets is guided by the Environmental and Energy Management
Policy, which mandates the assessment of its activities’ impact on
biodiversity and the implementation of measures to mitigate
effects on protected areas, species, and habitats. This policy is put
into practice through the following actions:
• any deforestation for new RES project purposes must be
compensated by equivalent afforestation in other areas
• prior to the commencement of projects, a detailed
environmental impact assessment or an initial environmental
screening shall be carried out, where required by applicable
regulatory frameworks or based on an internal assessment by
Latvenergo employees, in cases where no such assessment is
mandated by regulation

• local communities’ access to natural resources and ecosystem
services

• the ‘avoid-reduce-compensate’ hierarchy must be adhered to
all new RES projects

• the preservation of traditional economic activities and ways of life

• the siting of new RES assets shall be ensured outside
biologically valuable forest stands

• recreational opportunities and landscape quality
